TOBACCO: INDUSTRY SHOULD WIN HIGH STAKES POKER GAME
KEY POINTS:
President Clinton announced in the State of the Union that the DOJ will pursue a Federal
reimbursement lawsuit against the tobacco industry to recoup its health care expenditures
associated with tobacco use.
While the President's action is both surprising and disappointing, largely because we believe
that such a claim is unlikely to survive an industry motion to dismiss, we are maintaining our
Strong Buy rating on MO.
However, tobacco stocks will likely be under pressure in the short-term. We also realize that
it will take somewhat longer than we had hoped for tobacco stocks to reflect their underlying
value, and that tobacco issues will now remain on the "front page."
We believe that Clinton's move largely reflects a strategic political appeal to liberal
Democrats, rather than the underlying strength of such a claim. We are reducing our 12-
month target price on MO rom $73 (15% discount to the market) to $67 (25% discount to
the market).
Greatest threat: if the industry were unsuccessful in largely dismissing a Federal
reimbursement action prior to trial, the industry would likely be forced to settle such a claim
(given its scale; realistically the industry cannot try a case with such a large damage claim).
A reasonable worst-case scenario is to imagine a second Medicaid-like settlement (i.e., a
$0.45 per- pack price hike).
Consistent with our somewha: out of consensus view, we believe that a pending Federal
claim, from a practical perspective, will likely bar the spin-off of material non-tobacco
assets.
We maintain a Strong Buy rating on MO ($50), an outperform rating on BAT ($9 7/8), and a
Neutral rating on RN ($28), UST ($32), and MPP ($9).
